trust_decision.summary: Peer-controlled stream IDs decide how many entries stay in the per-connection streams hash. On CLOSED, stream_state only strips most keys and keeps the entry, so nothing bounds the table's growth.

landing_point.why: The summary names stream_state and the closed-stream cleanup. The CLOSED branch there deletes keys but never the streams entry.

fix_sites.entry_point: Protocol::HTTP2::Server/Client->feed -> Frame::frame_decode -> Connection::state_machine -> stream_state(CLOSED); also the send path via enqueue
Protocol::HTTP2::Connection->new (via Server->new / Client->new), new closed_streams/max_closed_streams fields
Connection->new option list, max_closed_streams becomes a constructor option

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix is one logical change in stream_state (fix.diff:100-110). The Connection.pm and Constants.pm hunks are only the constant and constructor plumbing (fix.diff:55-70, fix.diff:77-92).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Refused streams never reach CLOSED or enter stream_state, so a solver can argue that 'closed streams never removed' does not cover them and that the RST_STREAM send path is a 'REFUSED_STREAM special case' already handled by Connection.pm:207.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Closed-stream entries are kept on purpose, so late PRIORITY/WINDOW_UPDATE/RST frames on a closed stream are tolerated by the CLOSED branch, and PRIORITY can depend on a closed stream. Deleting the entry at close makes those frames reach new_peer_stream with id < last_peer_stream (connection PROTOCOL_ERROR), or makes stream_reprio fail with 'Malformed priority frame'.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A refused peer stream (MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS exceeded) queues RST_STREAM. state_machine then reads $self->{streams}->{$id}->{state} for a nonexistent id, which autovivifies an empty entry that never reaches CLOSED, so the new closed_streams cap never evicts it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The leak is an autovivification at Connection.pm:204 in another file, on a path the code labels as a 'REFUSED_STREAM error' early return (Connection.pm:206-207). It is not a 'closed stream', so it reads as outside the advisory's wording.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Stream.pm:56-61 -> Connection.pm:135-140 enqueue -> Connection.pm:202-207 state_machine; 2 files from the landing point, same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Any local enqueue (send_headers/send_data/RST via stream_error) for a stream id missing from the table hits the same autovivifying read in state_machine and adds a permanent empty entry outside the closed_streams accounting.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Mostly application-driven (Server->response with a bad stream_id). It is peer-driven only through the refused-stream route above.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Connection.pm, 1 file from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A client-side promised stream that is reset or refused before RESERVED and leaves an entry outside the closed_streams accounting.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PUSH_PROMISE creates peer streams through a separate decoder, and a maintainer could add a refusal/cleanup branch there that drops the entry without going through stream_state.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: IDLE peer streams created by a PRIORITY frame alone stay IDLE forever and never enter closed_streams. Today they are capped only by active_peer_streams.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RFC 7540 says lower IDLE ids are implicitly closed when a higher id opens, and a maintainer implementing that could mark them closed without pushing them to closed_streams.

O9_family: CWE-401 / unbounded per-connection state growth (resource exhaustion)
